Why this model: Simplest baseline: any model must beat "same month last year".
The current method used by the team, so it is the benchmark to improve on.
Parameters: CF = f(TWAP) with a and b per season (curve_fit), because the TWAP-CF link differs by season.

Why this model: Transparent: coefficients show how each input moves CF.
Linear model with shrinkage: inputs are correlated (e.g. twap_neg, month_cos) and there are only 36 training months.
Parameters:
alpha = 10 (WIND)/ 1 (SOLAR), chosen by RidgeCV (15 values, 1-100) on FY23-25 only.
A larger alpha means stronger shrinkage and a more stable fit.

Why this model: Captures non-linear effects and price-weather interactions without scaling the inputs.
Parameters: n_estimators = 300, max_depth = 4, min_samples_leaf = 2. Shallow trees and a minimum leaf size limit overfitting on 36 rows. 300 trees give a stable average.

Why this model: Boosted trees: non-linear like RF but learns from earlier errors.
Parameters:
n_estimators = 250, max_depth = 3, learning_rate = 0.05, subsample = 1.0, colsample_bytree = 1.0, reg_lambda = 1.0.
Small steps, shallow trees and random sampling keep it regularised.

Why this model: Averaging two different tree models reduces the error of each one.
Parameters: Mean of the RF and XGBoost predictions.
